findings.reason: the plan builds its whole repair on "an answered pick chose a lane the node does not fit", a branch that never ran, so a node dispatched with this brief aims at code the incident never reached.
findings.text: s23 says "The router, Jev, answered with `clive` (action `route`)", but the pick-timing record for that node (`an-admission-pass-reads-each-project-once`, project reckon) holds four attempts, at 02:29:07Z, 02:30:52Z, 02:31:37Z and 02:34:43Z on 3 November, every one reading `outcome: refuse`, `decision_source: refused`, `fallback_reason: no-eligible-candidates; default-backend-ineligible`, and none of them a `route`; the same record lists clive among the excluded with reason `context-fit`, so clive was never offered and the router never answered with it — the refusal the plan is repairing came from a pick that found no eligible candidate at all

findings.reason: part one adds what exists and part two guards a case the picker cannot produce, so the observed failure (a `refuse` answer that skips the reroute and lands on local) would survive the node as written.
findings.text: s23's first deliverable ("The candidate scan the router reads carries the node's context estimate") is already true at the base revision: `dispatch_picker.py:517` measures the estimate into the `PickRequest`, `picker/__init__.py:420` carries it through `snapshot_request`, and `picker/snapshot.py:787` charges `request.estimated_context` against each candidate's window — the failing dispatch's own record confirms it, holding `estimated_context: 234021` on every refusal — while the second deliverable ("when the router's answer is a lane the node does not fit") cannot occur, because that same check at `snapshot.py:787` keeps an oversized lane out of the offered set, and the action that did happen (`refuse`) is not router-free under `_router_free_resolution` (`dispatch.py:578-600`, which treats only `fallback` as a validated pick's answer)

findings.reason: without the `competence` reason in the control, the node can pass its own gate while leaving the waiver as unfireable as it was.
findings.text: s23's second case ("the router's scan built from its real estimate is offered codex by the picker itself, through the waiver") and its control ("Dropping the estimate from the router's scan fails the second") name the wrong mechanism: the estimate is already in the scan, and the waiver fails to fire because `_excluded_only_on_context` (`picker/snapshot.py:1402-1406`) requires every reason on every unreserved candidate to begin `context-fit: `, while the record shows the only unreserved lane carried `competence` as well — so the arm fails at base for a reason the unit neither states nor controls, and the named control cannot show the unit's change is what makes it pass
